newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures erased earlier losses after a much awaited speech by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan failed to meet traders worst fears, pushing the contract back into positive territory.
Traders said prices had drifted lower going into the speech, which started at 1500 GMT, but in the end there was little for the bears to latch onto.

Concerns about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin weighed slightly on Bunds and the French bond future earlier in the session although some traders were sceptical about how seriously they would be hit in the event of a shift in power.
"There was nothing there, that was the point," Nick Stephens at Credit Lyonnais Rouse said. "The bottom line is that the Fed looks its going to be reactive not proactive."

A head trader at a French brokerage said, "I don't really understand the reaction of the markets that well. They were scared by the first few comments before turning in the opposite direction. Greenspan told us the U.S. economy had good growth without inflation, but we knew that already."
We would have liked him to tell us how long that will last but there we're still in the dark," he said.
The bond future managed to come close to Monday's high early in the session, hitting 130.78 before steadily declining to a session low of 130.22. It eventually settled at 130.54, up 0.06.

Traders said the strong early performance was driven partly by switching out of Bunds into French bond futures by one U.S. house. "It looked like someone who was long (Bunds, short French bonds) getting out of their position as they'd had enough," said a trader at a large French brokerage.
French 10-year bond yields moved as much as 20 basis points below their German equivalents from minus 16 on Monday before stabilising at 17 basis points below.
Traders said March PIBOR suffered a late hit from a U.S. fund which appeared to be taking profits. Several large sales, in an otherwise quiet day, pushed the contract to 96.77 from 96.82 earlier.

However they also said the selling, while relatively large, was simply met by a wave of buyers on the other side still expecting rate cuts. The selling continued on the GLOBEX session but the contract recovered to 96.79.
"Don't read too much into it, there's a wall of buying under PIBOR," Stephens at Lyonnais Rouse said. He said June was even better supported, at 96.80/82, than the March contract.
"80/82 is impenetrable. People think even if we don't get anything by March we'll get it by June," he said.

Hopes for further rate cuts in Europe were helped on Tuesday by a surprise drop in the German Ifo business climate index in December. Traders said German M3 and the cost of living index, both due this week, would be the next main focus for the market.

The surprise of the day was the announcement of a 10 billion franc domestic bond issue by French welfare debt repayment fund CADES. It said it would sell October 12, 2000 bonds on Wednesday morning with a spread from four to six basis points over governmemt bonds. The coupon has yet to be determined.
